entries.classical_locus: Books I, II, IV, V, VI, VII Prefaces
entries.topic: Epistolary prefaces to Eudemus and Attalus dividing Books I–IV (elementary foundation, ἀγωγὴ στοιχειώδης) from Books V–VIII (special extensions, περιουσιαστικώτερα).
Generation of the arbitrary oblique scalene circular double cone, axial triangle, parallel circular sections (I.4), and antiparallel subcontrary circular sections (I.5, I.9).
Fundamental symptom of the Parabola (παραβολή): cutting plane parallel to a generator of the axial triangle yields QV² = PL · PV (y² = px), exact application of area.
Fundamental symptom of the Hyperbola (ὑπερβολή): cutting plane meeting both napes yields QV² = PV · PL + (PL/PP') PV², application exceeding by a figure similar to d × p.
Fundamental symptom of the Ellipse (ἔλλειψις): cutting plane meeting all generators of one nape yields QV² = PV · PL − (PL/PP') PV², application falling short by a figure similar to d × p.
Opposite branches (αἱ ἀντικείμεναι) cut from the double cone have equal latus rectum and form a single two-branched curve with center bisecting PP' and secondary conjugate diameter.
Tangent construction and harmonic division: TP = PV for the parabola (I.33, 35) and TP : TP' = PV : VP' (equivalently CT · CV = CP²) for central conics (I.34, 36–37).
Invariance of the conic symptom under transformation from the original cone-derived diameter to any new diameter QQ' and tangent at Q.

Construction of asymptotes (PL² = ¼ p·d), proof of non-intersection, bisected tangent segment LL' at P (II.3, 9), equal secant intercepts RQ = Q'R' (II.8, 16), asymptotic equation xy = const (II.12), and indefinite approach (II.14).
Opposite branches and conjugate hyperbolas share common asymptotes; conjugate diameters of original hyperbola swap transverse and secondary roles on the conjugate hyperbola.
Finding a diameter, center, and principal orthogonal axes of a given conic; constructing tangents from an external point by harmonic division and compass-and-straightedge.
Ratio of rectangles under segments of intersecting chords PO·OQ : RO·OS equals the ratio of squares on parallel tangents—generalizing Euclid III.35–36 (power of a point) from circles to all conics.
Harmonic properties of poles and polars: any secant through pole T is divided harmonically by the conic at R, R' and the chord of contact (polar) Qq at M: TR : TR' = MR : MR'.

Focal properties of central conics ('points arising out of the application', AS·SA' = b²): optical reflection equality (III.48 [Prop. 71]), pedal auxiliary circle (III.49 [Prop. 72]), and constant sum/difference SP ± S'P = AA' = 2a (III.51–52 [Prop. 73]).
Projective product of tangent intercepts and synthetic key to the Three-Line and Four-Line Locus of Euclid, Apollonius, Pappus (Book VII), and Descartes (La Géométrie, 1637).
Converse harmonic polar construction of tangents from an external point across single-branch and opposite-branch hyperbolas.

Two distinct conics cannot share an arc (IV.24 [Prop. 77]), intersect in at most four points (IV.25, 38, 43, 55 [Props. 78–83]), and if tangent at one point meet in at most two others—the ancient foundation of Bézout's theorem (2 × 2 = 4) and five-point conic uniqueness.

Minimum and maximum straight lines from axis points to a conic; constant parabola subnormal NG = ½ p_a (V.13, 27) and central-conic subnormal proportion NG : CN = p_a : AA' (V.14–15, 28–29); perpendicularity of minimum/maximum lines to the tangent (normals).

Exact diorismos of the number of normals through an arbitrary point O (2, 3, or 4 normals), determining point-by-point the evolute envelope of every conic and constructing normal feet via an auxiliary rectangular hyperbola.

Congruence and similarity of conic sections and segments: all parabolas are similar (VI.11 [Prop. 115]); central conics are similar iff their figures d × p are similar (VI.12–13 [Prop. 116]); embedding any given conic inside a prescribed right cone (VI.28–30 [Props. 120–122]).

Apollonius's First and Second Conjugate Diameter Theorems: (1) PP'² ± DD'² = AA'² ± BB'² (a'² ± b'² = a² ± b²); (2) area of circumscribed conjugate parallelogram LL'MM' equals rectangle of axes AA' · BB' (a'b' sin ω = ab).
Extrema and monotonic variations of d' ± d'', d'·d'', p', and d'² ± p'² across conjugate diameters, forged explicitly as diorismos machinery for the lost Book VIII.

entries.heath_prop: Intro Part II, Ch. I & Viète (1600)
entries.topic: Apollonius's On Tangencies: the ten contact problems (PPP through CCC, up to 8 tangent circles), reconstructed by Viète's Apollonius Gallus (1600) and connected to ETC X(181) (Apollonius Point).

Apollonius's Plane Loci Book II: the locus PA : PB = k (k ≠ 1) is the Circle of Apollonius on harmonic diameter H_in H_ex; the three Apollonius circles of a triangle form a coaxal pencil intersecting at the Isodynamic Points X(15) and X(16), alongside Cutting Off of a Ratio, Determinate Section, and Inclinations.
